articles.title: Local folder search vs a web agent search API
articles.question: How do I let an agent search a folder on my laptop instead of crawling the web?
articles.summary: Exa, Tavily and Firecrawl take a query or a URL and answer from the public web. XERJ takes a folder already on your disk and never opens a network connection.

articles.title: XERJ compared with ripgrep for code agents
articles.question: Is ripgrep enough for a coding agent, or do I need a code index?
articles.summary: 30 disclosed tasks on one 331-file code tree. The two tools agree on 18. ripgrep wins 5 named tasks outright, including a substring inside an identifier.

articles.title: XERJ vs ast-grep — syntax search and an index
articles.question: ast-grep vs a code index for an agent?
articles.summary: ast-grep wins structural rewriting and XERJ does none of it. For an agent the honest recommendation is to install both and give each the job it was built for.

articles.title: DocFetcher compared with XERJ for document search
articles.question: What is a free DocFetcher alternative that an agent can call?
articles.summary: DocFetcher is a desktop search GUI with a portable index and Outlook PST support. XERJ is a search engine an agent calls. A capability comparison, with no benchmark.

articles.title: HoudahSpot compared with XERJ for file search
articles.question: HoudahSpot vs a local search engine I can script?
articles.summary: HoudahSpot is a power-user front end for Spotlight, with hundreds of attribute filters. XERJ is a folder index an agent calls. No Mac run stands behind this page.

articles.title: Recoll compared with XERJ for document search
articles.question: What is the best local desktop search for a folder of PDFs and docs?
articles.summary: Recoll is a desktop search application with a GUI, email indexing and OCR hooks. XERJ is a search engine an agent calls. A capability comparison, with no benchmark.

articles.title: ripgrep-all compared with XERJ for PDFs and docs
articles.question: How do I grep PDFs and Word docs from the command line?
articles.summary: ripgrep-all wraps ripgrep with adapters for PDF, Office files, archives and SQLite. XERJ indexes the same folder for an agent. A capability comparison, no benchmark.

articles.title: Spotlight compared with XERJ for folder content
articles.question: Spotlight can't find text inside my project files. What else is there?
articles.summary: Spotlight is the Mac's system-wide index with zero setup and wide metadata. XERJ is a folder index an agent queries. A capability comparison, run on no Mac.

articles.title: XERJ vs LocalSynapse for MCP local file search
articles.question: What's a local MCP search engine for Claude?
articles.summary: Two local MCP search engines. LocalSynapse wins the desktop experience and formats XERJ has no extractor for. XERJ wins data files and the Elasticsearch REST API.

articles.title: XERJ vs Elasticsearch run on one machine
articles.question: Is there an Elasticsearch-compatible engine that isn't Elasticsearch?
articles.summary: The published board is 55 wins, 26 ties, 4 losses and 3 not-applicable across 88 cells against Elasticsearch 8.13.4. All 4 losses are read p99 under a write flood.

articles.title: XERJ vs Omnisearch for an Obsidian vault
articles.question: How do I search an Obsidian vault from outside Obsidian?
articles.summary: Omnisearch wins inside Obsidian and reaches images and PDFs through Text Extractor. XERJ reads the vault folder outside the editor. No head-to-head was run here.

articles.title: XERJ vs Khoj for searching your own documents
articles.question: What's a simpler alternative to Khoj if I only need search and memory?
articles.summary: Khoj is a whole self-hosted assistant: chat, custom agents, scheduled research and image generation. XERJ is the smaller piece, the search and memory engine.

articles.title: XERJ vs Meilisearch for local and agent search
articles.question: What's a local alternative to Meilisearch that indexes a folder by itself?
articles.summary: A local alternative to Meilisearch that reads a folder of mixed files by itself. Meilisearch wins typo tolerance by default. No head-to-head was run here.

articles.title: XERJ vs Typesense when the corpus is a folder
articles.question: Do I need Typesense for an agent to search my docs?
articles.summary: Typesense wins faceted product browsing and says so in its own use cases. An agent can query a folder of mixed files without it. No faceting test was run here.

articles.title: XERJ vs Pagefind for a folder of saved HTML
articles.question: Pagefind vs indexing a local HTML dump for an agent?
articles.summary: Pagefind wins static-site search in the browser with no server. XERJ indexes a local HTML dump on disk so an agent can query it. No head-to-head was run here.

articles.title: Search API or Qdrant for agent memory?
articles.question: Should my agent call a search API or a vector store?
articles.summary: Agent memory lives in the index process XERJ already runs, so no second data service starts. On 8 judged queries hybrid linear fusion scored precision@3 0.4583.
